meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did Owen get a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What do you have?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. People draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did you ask Owen about this before you entered the zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A misremembered line isn't a confession. Students get quotations wrong all the time.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, and I want that in writing.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
An outline is a plan, and writers change their argument as they go.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. A private rewrite before December 1, the mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, and I'll accept it to put this behind him. Tonight, in writing, with the principal copied.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. Put the time and the room in the email, and he'll be there.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday, November 12 after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record under procedure 4.4. I still expect that confirmed in writing, along with the time and the room, and I want the written apology for how the zero was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with nothing on his record; she still wants the written confirmation, the time and room, and an apology for the zero, and this is the fair outcome under 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the fabricated Hamlet quotation and answered her misquote defence by saying it wasn't close to anything in the play, because it was specific, checkable and tied to Owen's own essay.
What cost ground: Nothing clearly cost you ground, though the question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was never answered, and she may carry that into her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placing the edits at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM the night before the due date came very close to that night, which is why she went shorter and harder, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero, answer it directly in a sentence, since an open procedural question like that is where she would dig in if the meeting ran longer.
